1. Find a usage of `@NeedsTest`: https://github.com/ankidroid/Anki-Android/blob/main/AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/annotations/NeedsTest.kt
   a. Ensure that the method(s) you are testing are in use. 
3. Post the test(s) that you're handling on this issue, so people don't duplicate work
4. Write a unit test (`/test`, not `/androidTest`)
5. Ensure that re-introducing the bug or issue would break the test
6. Submit a Pull Request

title: Reorganizing the code tree.
body:
I'd love to do some cleanup in the code tree. I find it very confusing, even after almost 3 years working in it.

Right now, this issue is up for discussion, we are not expecting anyone to do anything until there is a consensus. The first question is whether you agree that it's, on principle, something worth doing, whether you oppose it, or whether you don't care (I'm not asking whether you want to work on it yourself, I'm fine doing it myself, or getting help of whoever people also belive it'll improve the state of the codebase and contributors work)

If we agree that it's worth doing a change, I suggest a new organization of the tree in https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IfEdbSWqWdpWWZUkFiENqty7twAupyJou7JakDvHkEo/edit?usp=sharing
I believe a design document is better than an issue because anyone can comment any specific point, and we can track discussions of each directory proposal independently.

**Implement View Binding**
Advantages of using it over findViewById
Null safety – Properties in the generated class are non-null. In the case of multiple layout versions, e.g. layout file for different screen orientation or size, if some configuration contains an id that is not present in others, the generated property will be nullable.
Type safety – Binding properties will be correctly typed, even with custom views.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I will try to implement ViewiBinding for all activities and fragments.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This issue can be marked as good first issue so it will be helpful for new contributors. I will make a readme for this issue which have all the information about how to implement viewBinding for activities and fragments .

**Additional context**
**Advantages**
Interoperability – Generated classes are in Java and are optimized for Kotlin-Java interoperability.
Injection capability – Generated class can be injected in activity or fragment.
Speed – There are no impacts on build speed, as it doesn’t use an annotation processor. After the first build with View Binding is enabled, it will dynamically generate new properties. And if you add new view elements to your XML, there is no need to rebuild every time

title: [Cleanup]: Fix Android Studio Warnings
body:
This task is designed as a small, useful task to onboard new users to the codebase who are unsure about what  to work on.

> [!IMPORTANT] 
> **Unique constraint to this issue**
> Multiple pull requests from the same author will not be accepted, unless the refactoring is part of a larger piece of work 

> [!TIP]
> You do not need to be assigned this issue to work on it

Android Studio flags a number of warnings in the AnkiDroid project.

If a file which contains these warnings is committed, then Android Studio will warn the author. If the warning was not introduced by the author's commit, then the author is unnecessarily slowed down by having to confirm that they did not introduce more warnings into the codebase (which inevitably leads them to disabling the warning, as they're low value).

The list of warnings can be obtained via:
* Code -> Inspect Code

![Screenshot 2023-02-16 at 21 38 16](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62114487/219492902-6f1198ee-50ed-4cf5-9d7b-95816653d8e8.png)

The aim of this task is to introduce new contributors to the code with an 'easy' first issue to resolve.

1. Run `Code -> Inspect Code` on the solution (it will be slow)
2. Select one file which has warnings (under the `Kotlin` header is easiest.- many of the Java warnings are not flagged by the IDE)
3. Fix all the errors, warnings + weak warnings in the file, automatically if this is offered by the IDE, or manually otherwise.
4. Produce a Pull Request

If you have completed this and desire to do more work, please select one of our accepted issues, [or fix some `@NeedsTest` annotations in the codebase.](https://github.com/ankidroid/Anki-Android/issues/13283)

Once this issue has been completed, we can use CI to run Android Studio in headless mode to ensure that the codebase gets to, and stays at 0 warnings.

title: Memory leak in SharedDecksActivity (suspected WebView Context issue)
body: ### Checked for duplicates? - [x] This issue is not a duplicate ### Does it also happen in the desktop version? - [ ] This bug does not occur in the latest version of Anki Desktop ### What are the steps to reproduce this bug? 1. Open AnkiDroid. 2. Navigate to "Get Shared Decks" (SharedDecksActivity). 3. Press the back button to return to the DeckPicker. 4. Repeat steps 1-3 multiple times (e.g., 10-20 times). 5. Inspect the memory usage using the Android Studio Profiler. **Observation** The memory usage keeps increasing. Instances of SharedDecksActivity are not being garbage collected. The heap dump suggests that UiModeManager holds a reference to the WebView, which in turn holds the Activity Context. I did it 7 times I did it 24 times ### Expected behaviour SharedDecksActivity should be garbage collected after it is destroyed. ### Debug info ```text AnkiDroid Version = 2.24.0alpha0-debug (120ae9e3e1cc9d74ae1cd9c93f87cf18d6a122d9) Backend Version = 0.1.62-anki25.09.2 (25.09.2 3890e12c9e48c028c3f12aa58cb64bd9f8895e30) Android Version = 14 (SDK 34) ProductFlavor = play Device Info = Google | google | emu64xa | sdk_gphone64_x86_64 | sdk_gphone64_x86_64 | ranchu Webview User Agent = Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 14; sdk_gphone64_x86_64 Build/UE1A.230829.036.A4; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/113.0.5672.136 Mobile Safari/537.36 ACRA UUID = cb9112dd-e24d-4e60-b2e8-a126d16276e7 FSRS = 5.1.0 (Enabled: false) Crash Reports Enabled = false AnkiDroid Version = 2.24.0alpha0-debug (120ae9e3e1cc9d74ae1cd9c93f87cf18d6a122d9) Backend Version = 0.1.62-anki25.09.2 (25.09.2 3890e12c9e48c028c3f12aa58cb64bd9f8895e30) Android Version = 15 (SDK 35) ProductFlavor = play Device Info = Google | google | emu64xa | sdk_gphone64_x86_64 | sdk_gphone64_x86_64 | ranchu Webview User Agent = Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 15; sdk_gphone64_x86_64 Build/AE3A.240806.036; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/141.0.7390.122 Mobile Safari/537.36 ACRA UUID = d3ddc623-c774-4c20-b707-be5792040f43 FSRS = 5.1.0 (Enabled: false) Crash Reports Enabled = false ``` ### (Optional) Anything else you want to share? I have been investigating this issue and I would like to share my findings and a potential solution for review. My Analysis: It seems that defining the WebView in the XML layout causes it to be initialized with the Activity Context. This appears to prevent the Activity from being garbage collected because system services (like UiModeManager) keep a reference to the WebView. Also there is no onDestory function in SharedDecksActivity. Experimental Fix: I tried modifying the code to instantiate the WebView programmatically using the Application Context instead of the Activity Context. Added onDestroy(): Explicitly calling webView.stopLoading(), clearing the webViewClient, and calling webView.destroy(). Replaced in XML with a FrameLayout container. Initialized WebView(applicationContext) in onCreate and added it to the container. Cleaned up the WebView in onDestroy. Result: In my tests (API 34, 35), this change stopped the memory leak. Request for Review: As I am a student and new to this codebase, I am not entirely sure if using applicationContext for the WebView might introduce other side effects (e.g., theming or dialog issues). Could you please review if this approach is correct/safe? ### Research - [x] I have checked the [manual](https://ankidroid.org/docs/manual.html) and the [FAQ](https://github.com/ankidroid/Anki-Android/wiki/FAQ) and could not find a solution to my issue - [ ] (Optional) I have confirmed the issue is not resolved in the latest alpha release ([instructions](https://docs.ankidroid.org/manual.html#betaTesting))

title: Define guidelines & processes for LLM/AI-based contributions
body:
I'm opening this issue for discussion. There have been a few comments on Discord (and the GSoC Mentor Summit/Mailing List). The burden on reviewers is steadily increasing, but the meaningful benefit from LLM-generated Pull Requests doesn't justify this additional burden.

The aim is to:

* Define our current problems
* Research what other orgs are doing for these problems
* Brainstorm reasonable solutions

**Outcomes**

I don't want to be heavy-handed here, a few incremental changes will likely suffice. I suspect that this will result in some of:

* An update to our [PR Template](https://github.com/ankidroid/Anki-Android/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md)
* An 'acceptable use' policy for LLM-based contributions 
* Potential configuration changes to GitHub Copilot
* An update to [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/ankidroid/Anki-Android/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
